arxiv-2011-08018.creator: Rosana El Jurdi, Caroline Petitjean, Paul Honeine, Veronika Cheplygina, Fahed Abdallah
arxiv-2011-08018.description: Abstract Today, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated state of the art performance for supervised medical image segmentation, across various imaging modalities and tasks. Despite early success, segmentation networks may still generate anatomically aberrant segmentations, with holes or inaccuracies near the object boundaries.

arxiv-2112-02670.title: Momentum scalar triple product as a measure of chirality in electron ionization dynamics of strongly-driven atoms
arxiv-2112-02670.creator: G. P. Katsoulis, Z. Dube, P. Corkum, A. Staudte, A. Emmanouilidou
arxiv-2112-02670.description: Abstract We formulate a transparent measure that quantifies chirality in single electron ionization triggered in atoms, which are achiral systems. We do so in the context of Ar driven by a new type of optical fields that consists of two non-collinear laser beams giving rise to chirality that varies in space across the focus of the beams.

arxiv-2304-12179.title: Classical mechanics with inequality constraints
arxiv-2304-12179.creator: Andrei Frolov, Valeri P. Frolov
arxiv-2304-12179.description: Abstract In this paper we discuss mechanical systems with inequality constraints. We demonstrate how such constraints can be taken into account by proper modification of the action which describes the original unconstrained dynamics. To illustrate this approach we consider a harmonic oscillator in the model with limiting velocity.

arxiv-2310-17962.title: A Markov theorem for plat closure of surface braids in Dunwoody and periodic Takahashi manifolds
arxiv-2310-17962.creator: Alessia Cattabriga, Paolo Cavicchioli
arxiv-2310-17962.description: Abstract In this article we deal with the problem of finding equivalence moves for links in Dunwoody and periodic Takahashi manifolds. We represent these manifolds using Heegaard splitting and we represent the embedded links as plat closure of elements in the braid group of the corresponding Heegaard surfaces.

arxiv-2401-01946.title: Generation of gauge magnetic fields in a kagome spin liqud candidate using the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
arxiv-2401-01946.creator: Byungmin Kang and Patrick A. Lee
arxiv-2401-01946.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Byungmin Kang and Patrick A. Lee. The recent discovery of magnetization oscillations in a kagome spin liquid candidate motivates us to examine the origin of the gauge magnetic field term that can give rise to quantum oscillations of fermionic spinons. We find that in the presence of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and an average spin polarization, the spin permutation operator around the unit cell acquires an imaginary part, and a net gauge flux is generated through the unit cell of the kagome lattice.

arxiv-2407-05302.title: Mamba Hawkes Process for Event Sequence Modeling
arxiv-2407-05302.creator: Shan Dai, Yuyang Shen, Yuyang Liang, Chenhao Ma, Anningzhe Gao
arxiv-2407-05302.description: Abstract . Modeling asynchronous event sequences is crucial in numerous real-world applications such as healthcare monitoring, financial transaction analysis, and so on. Traditional temporal point processes, including Hawkes Processes, often fail to capture complex dependencies due to their parametric limitations. While neural approaches like RNNs and Transformers have improved flexibility, they struggle with computational inefficiency, and attention saturation.

arxiv-2409-12634.title: Exploring bat song syllable representations in self-supervised audio encoders
arxiv-2409-12634.creator: Marianne de Heer Kloots, Mirjam Knörnschild
arxiv-2409-12634.description: Abstract How well can deep learning models trained on human-generated sounds distinguish between another species’ vocalization types? We analyze the encoding of bat song syllables in several self-supervised audio encoders, and find that models pre-trained on human speech generate the most distinctive representations of different syllable types.

arxiv-2506-13028.title: NaSh: Guardrails for an LLM-Powered Natural Language Shell
arxiv-2506-13028.creator: Bimal Raj Gyawali, Saikrishna Achalla, Konstantinos Kallas, Sam Kumar
arxiv-2506-13028.description: Abstract . We explore how a shell that uses an LLM to accept natural language input might be designed differently from the shells of today. As LLMs may produce unintended or unexplainable outputs, we argue that a natural language shell should provide guardrails that empower users to recover from such errors.

arxiv-2510-01642.title: FailSafe: Reasoning and Recovery from Failures in Vision-Language-Action Models
arxiv-2510-01642.creator: Zijun Lin, Jiafei Duan, Haoquan Fang, Dieter Fox, Ranjay Krishna, Cheston Tan, Bihan Wen
arxiv-2510-01642.description: Abstract Recent advances in robotic manipulation have integrated low-level robotic control into Vision-Language Models (VLMs), extending them into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. Although state-of-the-art VLAs achieve strong performance in downstream robotic applications, supported by large-scale crowd-sourced robot training data, they still inevitably encounter failures during execution. Enabling robots to reason and recover from unpredictable and abrupt failures remains a critical challenge.

arxiv-2512-24898.title: PRISM : A Hierarchical Multiscale Approach for Time Series Forecasting
arxiv-2512-24898.creator: Zihao Chen, Alexandre Andre, Wenrui Ma, Ian Knight, Sergey Shuvaev, Eva Dyer
arxiv-2512-24898.description: Abstract Forecasting is critical in areas such as finance, biology, and healthcare. Despite the progress in the field, making accurate forecasts remains challenging because real-world time series contain both global trends, local fine-grained structure, and features on multiple scales in between.

pmc-13267850.title: A Case of Advanced Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Showing Extreme Lumbosacral Nerve Root Hypertrophy
pmc-13267850.creator: John Paul Lemchak, Justin Brown-Gnarra, Christian Roberti, Murat Ibatullin
pmc-13267850.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease is the most common hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy. While diagnosis is typically established through clinical findings, nerve conduction studies (NCS), and genetic testing, imaging manifestations such as nerve root hypertrophy are increasingly recognized. This case report presents a 43-year-old man with lifelong progressive distal weakness who presented with severe lower extremity atrophy, pes cavus deformities, and wheelchair dependence. Neurologic examination revealed marked distal weakness and hyporeflexia, while nerve conduction studies demonstrated severely reduced sural nerve conduction velocity.

pmc-13542519.creator: Heonhak Ha, Jinseok Kong, Junhyung Kim, Jiwon Kang, Min Seok Jang
pmc-13542519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transmissive active metasurfaces are essential for ultra‐compact on‐chip optical systems and are widely used in sensing, imaging, and spectroscopy. However, these devices generally suffer from lower efficiency and greater design complexity compared to their reflective counterparts. In this work, an electrically tunable transmission filter based on single‐layer graphene integrated with a capacitive gold grating on a mid‐IR transparent CaF2 substrate is demonstrated.
